title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the Tannakian category M of motives over R, with Betti fibre functor T_B (via X(C)) and motivic Galois group G = Aut_⊗(T_B), an affine group scheme over Q.

(1) Real Frobenius. Complex conjugation x ↦ x̄ on X(C), for X smooth projective over R, acts on H*(X(C),Q). This is functorial and compatible with ⊗ (Künneth), so it defines a ⊗-automorphism of T_B, i.e. a point F_∞ ∈ G(Q) with F_∞² = 1. Grothendieck calls it the 'frobénius réel'.

(2) Real structures. Let σ_M be the complex conjugation of M⊗_Q C coming from the Q-structure M = T_B(M). The comparison T_DR(M)⊗_R C ≅ T_B(M)⊗_Q C gives a second real structure, with conjugation τ_M. The claim is τ_M = F_∞σ_M = σ_M F_∞. The two factors commute because F_∞ is Q-rational. Concretely, the de Rham real structure on H*(X(C),C) is the fixed space of 'pull back by conjugation, then conjugate coefficients'.

(3) The period torsor over R. P = Isom_⊗(T_B⊗_Q R, T_DR) is a right G_R-torsor. Its class in H¹(Gal(C/R), G(C)) is the cocycle sending the nontrivial element to F_∞. This is consistent with the previous page's relation ᾱ = F_∞α for the comparison point α ∈ P(C). The inner form of G_R defined by P, namely Aut_⊗(T_DR), is obtained by descending G_C along the twisted conjugation int(F_∞)∘σ_C.

(4) Compatibility with Hodge theory. Let j: S_R = Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R be the Deligne-torus homomorphism defining the Hodge structures. Then F_∞ j(λ) F_∞^{-1} = j(λ̄), where λ ↦ λ̄ is the canonical (complex-conjugation) automorphism of S_R. Equivalently, F_∞ exchanges H^{p,q} and H^{q,p} C-linearly.

Purpose: this sets up the structure (G, F_∞, j, real form) used on the surrounding pages. The previous page shows, under the Hodge conjecture, that F_∞ = 1 on ⟨M⟩, i.e. P has a real point and the field of periods R(α) is R, iff M is generated by Q(-2n). The next page studies F_∞ against the Weil element C = j(i), via normalizers and a maximal compact (Cartan involution) of the adjoint group. In short: the data of a 'real motivic Galois group with Frobenius at infinity', the germ of Deligne's 1979 formalism of F_∞ and real periods.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. One informality: the transcribed phrase 'la structure réelle sur les M ⊗_R C' should read M ⊗_Q C. The sentence 'on retrouve que f_∞ [détermine] la structure réelle' is elliptic.
Commutation F_∞σ_M = σ_M F_∞ is asserted without comment; it holds because F_∞ ∈ G(Q).
The boxed relation F_∞ j(λ) F_∞^{-1} = j(λ̄) is stated without proof. It follows from the fact that conjugation on X(C) is antiholomorphic, so F_∞* maps H^{p,q} to H^{q,p}. It is correct.

ideas.what: Complex conjugation on X(C) defines an element F_∞ of order ≤2 in the motivic Galois group G(Q) of motives over R ('Frobenius réel').
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979); folklore in the theory of L-function Γ-factors (Serre 1970)

ideas.what: The de Rham real structure on M⊗C has conjugation τ_M = F_∞σ_M.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of real structures / F_∞-twisted conjugation (real periods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1979 (§0–1); Beilinson-type real Hodge–de Rham structures

ideas.what: The period torsor P = Isom_⊗(T_B⊗R, T_DR) over R has class given by the cocycle with value F_∞. The de Rham real form of G is the inner twist of G_R by int(F_∞).
ideas.modern_name: Real period torsor; inner form of the motivic Galois group defined by the de Rham fibre functor over R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1979), Deligne–Milne 'Tannakian categories' (1982); Y. André, 'Une introduction aux motifs' (2004)

ideas.what: Compatibility F_∞ j(λ) F_∞^{-1} = j(λ̄) between real Frobenius and the Hodge cocharacter j: S_R → G_R.
ideas.modern_name: Real Hodge structure with involution F_∞ (F_∞ maps H^{pq} to H^{qp}); real Mumford–Tate data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971; 'Valeurs de fonctions L', 1979)

missed.claim: This page gives an early (c. 1969–72) explicit Tannakian formulation of motives over R. It has the real Frobenius as a Q-point of the motivic Galois group, the cohomology class of the real period torsor equal to F_∞, and the de Rham group as an inner twist. This predates Deligne's 1979 formalism of F_∞ and real periods. It is of historical interest rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: f_∞ ∈ G(Q) (f_∞² = 1). ("frobénius réel") … le 1-cocycle sur Γ = Z/2Z, à valeurs dans G(C), dont la valeur en l'élément ≠ e est f_∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's priority for the motivic-Galois-group viewpoint on real periods, F_∞ and the real period torsor. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (F_∞, the τ = F_∞σ relation, the torsor cocycle, the compatibility with h) is standard since Deligne 1979 and is routine to a specialist. The notable points are the early date and the explicit torsor/inner-twist formulation in Grothendieck's own hand. Combined with the neighbouring pages, which characterize F_∞ = 1 via even Tate twists and relate F_∞ to the Cartan involution, this gives modest historical interest.

'[M ∈ Ob Rep(G)]' — the image reads 'M ∈ Ob Rep(G)' with G looking like C/G; the meaning is M ∈ Ob Rep_Q(G).
In the last boxed formula the image shows j(λ̄) with a correction mark above λ; it is consistent with the stated automorphism λ ↦ λ' of S_R inducing λ ↦ λ̄ on S_R(R) ≅ C*.
